correctness.rationale: The exact coordinate identities and strict inward bounds hold for every point of the explicit cone. Reciprocal bounds yield global forward existence and L2(qx); the stable p-convolution yields L2(p-1), giving an integrable logarithmic derivative of J=x exp(q^2/8). Its positive limit is continuous and nonconstant by uniform tails and small-coordinate estimates. Gaussian-tail inversion yields the full log-log-plus-data clock, and stable forcing yields the universal 2/t correction. The actual standalone symbolic/numerical checker passed; numerical tests were not used for infinite proof.

value.rationale: The explicit positive nonconstant scattering coordinate is a natural asymptotic invariant for the noncompact escaping part of a polynomial system with a degenerate equilibrium line. It parametrizes the original-time height offset for different trajectories, while the log-log term and 2/t correction quantify behavior that the existing first-order escape law leaves undetermined. No global theorem or extensive classification is required for this narrow, structurally motivated invariant; unlike a routine numerical extra digit, existence and nonconstancy require an L2/L1 argument and record genuinely new initial-condition memory.
